messages.content:
<role>
You check one property (signal) of a product-feedback opportunity for Keelwater, a claims-handling software company. You do not rewrite anything.
</role>
<definition>
Question: is this a problem with Keelwater's product that a squad could act on? Pass means yes.
Fail if the cause is outside the product (pricing, contracts, the customer's own IT, staffing), if a help article would have answered it, or if it is praise.
A feature request or a described workaround is signal.
The evidence is the title, the problem statement and up to 12 customer quotes with route and date.
</definition>
<evidence>
{
 "title": "Joint policyholder names missing from letters",
 "problem_statement": "Letters sent to joint policyholders display only one name, often the wrong one, causing confusion and complaints. Customers expect both names to appear correctly, and the failure to do so damages trust and creates unnecessary friction.",
 "quotes": [
  {
   "quote": "they’re only pulling through one name, and it’s causing complaints",
   "route": "account_management",
   "date": "2026-09-29T13:22:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "Sure — when we generate letters for policies with two named holders, the system only pulls through one name, sometimes the wrong one.",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-10-29T10:16:00Z"
  },
  {
   "quote": "Hi Bryn, we’ve got a repeat issue where letters sent to joint policyholders are only showing one name — it’s causing confusion and complaints from customers.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-09-03T12:32:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "We’re getting complaints because when there are joint ... policyholder names, the system merges them incorrectly—sometimes ... showing one or the wrong one",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-10-07T14:03:00Z"
  },
  {
   "quote": "We’re getting complaints because the system isn’t merging both names correctly — it’s only showing one joint policyholder names, and customers are understandably upset.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-09-03T12:32:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "Appreciate you taking this seriously — we’ve had three complaints this month just because the joint policyholder names weren’t merged correctly.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-09-03T12:32:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "Hi Bryn, we’re getting complaints again because letters to joint policyholders only show one name — it’s causing real friction with clients.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-09-29T15:23:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "We’re seeing repeated issues where letters sent to joint policyholders only display one name — this leads to complaints and we need the joint policyholder names to appear correctly in all communications.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-09-29T15:23:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "We’re getting heat ... because the system isn’t handling joint policyholder names correctly — it’s pulling in just one, and that’s triggering formal complaints.",
   "route": "account_management",
   "date": "2026-09-29T13:22:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "That’s the issue — ... I’ll pull the ... cases for you.",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-09-26T14:35:00Z"
  },
  {
   "quote": "we’re getting complaints because our letters to joint policyholders only show one name — it’s causing confusion and we need this fixed.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-30T15:16:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "we’ve been having some trouble with joint policyholder names in outgoing letters",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-10-29T10:16:00Z"
  }
 ]
}
</evidence>
<task>
Write a critique of 2-5 sentences naming the claim, quote or item you checked and what you found. Then give the verdict. If any single item fails, the verdict is fail.
</task>
<output>
JSON only: {"critique": string, "verdict": "pass" | "fail"}
</output>

response.content: {"critique": "The claim is that Keelwater's letter generation only pulls through one joint policyholder name, sometimes the wrong one. Multiple quotes across support, sales, and account_management routes (Sep-Oct 2026) consistently describe the same product defect causing customer complaints, e.g. 'the system only pulls through one name, sometimes the wrong one' and 'letters to joint policyholders only show one name.' This is a product behavior a squad could fix, not a pricing, contract, or customer-side issue, and no help article would resolve it.", "verdict": "pass"}
